title: BLESS: Bandwidth and Locality Enhanced SMEM Seeding Acceleration for DNA Sequencing
problem: DNA sequence alignment's seeding process, which finds super-maximal exact matches (SMEM) between samples and reference genomes, is a major bottleneck due to memory-intensive characteristics. Current learned-index approaches lack spatial locality and suffer from random runtime access patterns, constraining memory bandwidth utilization.
motivation: DNA sequencing is critical for developing effective countermeasures against harmful viruses like COVID-19.
method: BLESS introduces a coarse-fine (CF) block data structure that maps seeding parameters to exploit spatial locality and increase effective bandwidth for high bandwidth memory (HBM). It develops the guaranteed search range update (GSRU) algorithm that exploits caching during search to enable temporal locality and data reuse. A multi-core accelerator architecture built on HBM employs context switching and runtime scheduling to maximize core and memory bandwidth utilization.
key_novelty: The CF block data structure combined with GSRU algorithm to enhance spatial and temporal locality in learned-index-based DNA seeding.
contributions: Coarse-fine (CF) block data structure for exploiting spatial locality and increasing effective bandwidth usage
Guaranteed search range update (GSRU) algorithm for enabling temporal locality and data reuse through caching
Multi-core seeding accelerator design with HBM integration, context switching, and intelligent runtime scheduling
35.65x speedup over BWA-MEME and 15.49x over ERT-ASIC in raw system performance
primary_theme: bandwidth and locality optimization for DNA seeding
